papers.citation: Gottman, Swanson & Murray (1999). The mathematics of marital conflict: Dynamic mathematical nonlinear modeling of newlywed marital interaction. Journal of Family Psychology 13(1):3-19

Gottman, Levenson, Swanson, Swanson, Tyson & Yoshimoto (2003). Observing gay, lesbian and heterosexual couples' relationships: Mathematical modeling of conflict interaction. Journal of Homosexuality 45(1):65-91

fidelity: computational reproduction of model properties and estimation procedure from published group-mean parameters; no couple data; model code imported from regesh.bonding.dyad

e1_structural.claim: for the sigmoidal influence function, we can have one, three, or five steady states; in most of our data there was only one influenced steady state per couple

e2_published.note: Published influenced steady states are group means of per-couple graphical estimates; the model couple built from mean parameters has the uninfluenced point as its interior fixed point whenever both uninfluenced means lie inside the thresholds, so coordinate-wise agreement within tolerance is only possible when the published influenced and uninfluenced means are themselves within tolerance.

e3_recovery.note: Bias and RMSE exclude replications where the zero subset had fewer than three points (fraction_none) and non-finite estimates. The comparison estimators fit a bilinear partner equation to ojive-generated data, so only inertia and uninfluenced steady state are comparable for them.

e4_repair_damping.claim: damping may create a positive-positive stable steady state where none existed before
